PullRequest.Title: sessions: Preserve default chat identity in partial summary updates
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Preserve the known default chat when `root/sessionSummaryChanged` includes an updated chat catalog but omits the unchanged `defaultChat` field. Prefer an explicitly advertised default chat over native URI conventions.

AHP summary notifications are partial updates: omitted fields retain their previous values. Copilot cloud host sends a new chat catalog when status changes, without resending an unchanged default-chat pointer. VS Code incorrectly classified the opaque primary chat URI as a peer, causing automatic fallback to that peer; detailed session state then restored the main chat. Repeated identity switches coincide with the reported Agents window layout blinking on messages and tool confirmations.

VS Code's own host uses the same partial-update semantics, but its `ahp-chat://default/...` naming convention masked the client bug. The fix belongs in the shared client rather than requiring cloud hosts to resend unchanged fields.

### CI

- `gh run list --repo microsoft/vscode --branch roblou/agents/agents-window-layout-issue-fix --limit 15 --json databaseId,headSha,status,conclusion,workflowName` — confirmed Telemetry and all other workflows succeeded on the exact head.

New regressions cover metadata-only and hydrated opaque default chats, alternating detailed-state/summary updates, real `VisibleSessions` automatic fallback, and explicitly changed default identity. The fallback regression reproduced six unwanted active-chat switches before the fix and none afterward.

Live cloud-session pane geometry has not been validated against a fixed application build. No issue has been filed.

(Written by Copilot)

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each partial catalog/status notification could replace the default chat with a peer and each detailed-state update replace it back, causing repeated active-chat fallback and synchronous layout/panel reconciliation on message and tool-confirmation status transitions.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Visible Agents-window layout blinking and redundant synchronous layout work during repeated session status updates.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The changed handler merges the cached backend default-chat URI into partial catalog notifications before reconciliation, so metadata/state updates retain the same main-chat object and no longer trigger active-chat fallback or downstream layout reconciliation. Explicitly supplied defaults still override the cached URI.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base handler passed partial `changes` directly to `chatMetadataFromSummary`; when `defaultChat` was omitted, an opaque advertised default failed `isDefaultChatUri`, was recreated as a peer, and removed the stable main chat from `session.chats`. `VisibleSessions` then synchronously fell back because its active chat was absent (visibleSessions.ts:985-995). Alternating detailed-state and summary updates reversed this identity on each update. The added regression test drives three status cycles and asserts a single active-chat publication, while layout consumers synchronously observe active-chat changes: ChatLayoutContext increments layout generations (chatLayout.ts:84-94), panel visibility/view synchronization reruns (baseSessionLayoutController.ts:360-421), and the desktop strategy reapplies session composition in multi-session mode (desktopExistingSessionStrategy.ts:141-174).

Scenarios.Scenario: A visible Agent Host session with an opaque default-chat URI receives partial `root/sessionSummaryChanged` catalog/status updates while messages or tool confirmations progress.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The already-received notification synchronously enters `_handleSessionSummaryChanged`, reads the cached default backend URI, maps the complete chat catalog, and commits one observable transaction before the sessions UI reacts. Catalog reconciliation remains O(C); the diff adds one O(1) cache/observable lookup and one URI string conversion. Hydrated detailed-state updates may alternate with summaries, but the fixed identity prevents active-chat fallback and downstream layout reapplication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive an existing Agent Host `root/sessionSummaryChanged` notification containing the replacement chat catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inbound notification per host summary/status change; catalog processing is one grouped operation for C advertised chats, not one IPC call per chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same notification was received and the same O(C) catalog reconciliation ran, but omitted `defaultChat` could oscillate chat identity and trigger repeated UI/layout observers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The notification has already crossed the boundary; local reconciliation must finish before observers publish the updated session state. The changed code performs no outbound IPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Maintain the existing per-session detailed-state subscription when chat details are observed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the existing one subscription for a hydrated/observed session; metadata-only sessions require none. The new tests assert no extra subscription is acquired.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same zero-or-one subscription lifecycle existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: State delivery can alternate with summary delivery, but the diff neither opens nor waits for a subscription in the changed handler.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The complete replacement chat catalog, with effective cardinality C after the host groups chats into one summary. Existing reconciliation allocates/maps O(C); the added preservation work is O(1) per notification plus URI-length string conversion.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Connection notifications are handled synchronously in listener order. The observable transaction coalesces publications for each notification; there is no new task fan-out, limiter, queue, or parallel boundary. Alternating state and summary events remain sequential.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The handler only runs for an entry already present in `_sessionCache`; a cache miss returns without work. On a warm entry, the cached default backend URI is read locally. No new cache key, miss retry, negative-cache behavior, retention, or invalidation path is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed handler, cache lookup, O(C) reconciliation, VisibleSessions fallback, and synchronous layout observers were directly traced; the regression test covers three alternating status cycles.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact notification frequency and catalog size vary by host, but the added cost is bounded and the removed layout churn occurs on each affected alternating update.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds negligible bounded local work and prevents repeated active-chat switches and synchronous layout reconciliation.

Scenarios.Scenario: A session is initially listed or explicitly changes its advertised default chat while its catalog contains URI shapes that also match local default conventions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The inbound full summary or explicit partial update maps the complete catalog and `applyChatMetadata` updates stable chat facades in one synchronous transaction. The changed predicate compares each catalog entry with the authoritative advertised default; mapping remains O(C), and explicit changes continue to override cached identity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive the existing Agent Host session-added or session-summary-changed payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inbound payload per add/change, containing one grouped catalog of C chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same inbound payload and O(C) projection occurred; the old predicate could classify both an explicit default and a convention-shaped chat as default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local catalog projection is on the UI-observable update path, but no new remote call is made or awaited by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: C chats in the host-provided catalog. The predicate remains constant work per chat, so total mapping remains O(C) with no cardinality increase.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous reconciliation per inbound notification with transaction-level observable coalescing; no per-chat async work or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Initial listing constructs the cache from the supplied full summary. Explicit updates use the supplied `defaultChat` because object spread precedence overrides the cached value. No additional persistence, cache population, or cache lifetime change occurs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both helper call sites and `applyChatMetadata` were inspected, including object-spread precedence for explicit defaults.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog sizes are host-dependent, but the algorithmic cost and boundary count are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Authoritative default selection changes classification semantics without adding boundary calls, retained state, or asymptotic work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. No diff-introduced performance finding was found. The production change adds only bounded local lookup/string work and fixes a prior synchronous UI/layout churn regression, which was recorded separately with its introducing commit.
